notes.claim: Capacitors and inductors absorb energy during one half-cycle and return it in the other, so the power wave goes below zero.
True power is measured in watts, reactive power in volt-amps reactive (VAR), and their combination is apparent power in volt-amps.
Power factor is true power divided by apparent power, which equals the cosine of the phase angle; average power is V I cos φ with rms values.
Any power factor less than 1 means the wiring must carry more current to deliver the same true power.

For i8: a generator is rated in kVA at a stated power factor, with a kW figure as well, so it is checked against both: 100 kVA supplies 80 kW at 0.8, and a 60 Hz diesel set's data sheet reads 630 kVA and 504 kW at 0.8.

sources.quote: The actual amount of power being used, or dissipated, in a circuit is called true power , and it is measured in watts (symbolized by the capital letter P, as always).

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 11
sources.quote: This “phantom power” is called reactive power , and it is measured in a unit called Volt-Amps-Reactive (VAR), rather than watts. The mathematical symbol for reactive power is (unfortunately) the capital letter Q.

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 11
sources.quote: Because true power and apparent power form the adjacent and hypotenuse sides of a right triangle, respectively, the power factor ratio is also equal to the cosine of that phase angle.

sources.quote: lagging power factor loads tend to demagnetize the field and terminal voltage is maintained only by increasing the d.c. field current. Therefore, a.c. generators are rated in terms of load current and voltage output, or kilovolt-ampere (kVA) output, at a specified frequency and power factor.

sources.title: maritime electrical installations - notes on design ...
sources.quote: a single phase a.c. generator designed to deliver 100 amperes at 1,000 volts is rated at 100 kVA. This machine would supply a 100 kW load at unity power factor or a 80 kW load at 80 percent power factor.
